source_review.notes: Checked CloudEvents 1.0.2, AsyncAPI 3.0.0, Apache Avro 1.12.0, JSON Schema Draft 2020-12, RFC 3339, the current OpenTelemetry Logs Data Model, W3C PROV-O, and W3C Trace Context. All eight cited destinations returned HTTP 200. Claims are limited to event-envelope context, message-driven API description, schema resolution, JSON validation, timestamp syntax, event/observed time, provenance, and trace propagation within each source's stated scope.

evidence: Reviewed the event-contract tuple, source-qualified deduplication identity, named-time symbols, and consumer transition function.
Checked separation of event, subject, command, causation, correlation, trace, delivery, and processing identities.
Verified that schema, payload, authority, provenance, controls, and lifecycle components have distinct meanings.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation preserves the boundary among domain occurrence, asserted event record, transported notification, consumer transition, and external effect.

evidence: Executed event-contract-integrity with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced 4 events, 0 valid events, 4 sorted findings, and ready=false.
Independently counted one intended failing predicate for payment-captured, customer-updated, inventory-adjusted, and order-cancelled.
Verified that valid counts events with no local findings and ready becomes true only when all four pass.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Counts are exact for the declared fixture and do not estimate delivery frequency, duplicate rates, clock error, or production correctness.

evidence: Re-derived stable retry identity as preservation of the source-plus-event-ID tuple while delivery attempts vary.
Checked semantic idempotency as F(F(s,e),e)=F(s,e) for the declared state effect and separated external side effects.
Reviewed the named-time ordering as a common pipeline expectation rather than a theorem under independent clocks, batching, and correction.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The symbolic results are scoped to declared identities, state transitions, clocks, and effects; they do not imply end-to-end exactly-once behavior.

evidence: Reviewed occurrence versus record versus notification versus message, fact versus command, domain versus change event, and event versus subject identity.
Tested duplicate retries, distinct duplicate facts, late and out-of-order data, sequence gaps, clock uncertainty, partition changes, unknown enums, schema defaults, and partial payload absence.
Reviewed false authority, corrections, retractions, compensation, dead letters, sensitive metadata, archive deletion, backfill overlap, replay side effects, and historic reducer drift.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary cases prevent schema validity, broker position, correlation, past-tense naming, or scoped transport guarantees from standing in for domain truth.

evidence: Traced event type and grain through subject identity, source, authority, occurrence time, causation, payload, schema, and provenance.
Verified duplicate, retry, ordering, idempotency, correction, compatibility, unknown-value, and consumer transition obligations.
Checked minimization, integrity, retention, dead letters, replay, backfill, recovery, metrics, drift, deprecation, and retirement across all ten gates.
invariant_checking.notes: The invariants preserve semantic identity and historical evidence across publication, delivery, processing, evolution, correction, and replay.

evidence: Reviewed the occurrence, identity-and-authority, time-and-provenance, information-model, schema-and-envelope, delivery-and-ordering, evolution, protection, replay-and-recovery, and lifecycle gates.
Checked counterexamples to every-message-is-event, past-tense-proves-fact, one-ID-is-enough, one-timestamp-is-enough, schema-valid-is-true, and replay-is-republishing reasoning.
Verified that acceptance requires authoritative semantics, versioned artifacts, consumer evidence, scoped guarantees, protected lifecycle, and correction/replay controls.
proof_review.notes: The chapter provides an event-contract assurance argument, not proof that one envelope, schema language, broker, retention policy, or delivery mechanism fits all systems.

evidence: Audited uses of event, fact, immutable, unique, ordered, exactly once, authoritative, valid, compatible, reproducible, required, and proof.
Confirmed that source assertions, transport properties, schema resolution, state idempotency, external effects, replay projections, and historical truth remain distinct.
Verified that the executable checker is labeled as four registry predicates and excludes occurrence truth, clock correctness, authority, delivery, processing, protection, or replay proof.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Claims remain bounded to exact event types, identity scopes, authorities, clocks, schemas/profiles, channels, consumers, effects, versions, and evidence.

evidence: Reviewed standards-backed mechanics, illustrative workflows, executable fixture output, producer-consumer tests, runtime metrics, replay exercises, and domain assertions as distinct evidence types.
Confirmed that no production delivery guarantee, event truth, compatibility rate, clock accuracy, security/privacy determination, safe replay, successful recovery, or external review is claimed.

Checked that local adoption requires representative events, authoritative fixtures, exact schemas and configurations, fault tests, operational measurements, protection review, replay rehearsal, and accountable approval.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Specifications, modeled semantics, generated fixtures, conformance tests, production observations, and outcome claims are explicitly distinguished.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed occurrence, event, notification, message, semantic grain, layered contracts, type and identity, authority, time, causality, payload styles, absence, schemas, defaults, enums, compatibility, ordering, idempotency, correction, publication, channels, protection, retention, replay, backfill, observability, and lifecycle as one coherent discipline.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable event registries, envelope and payload fields, schema bindings, producer-consumer matrices, duplicate stores, ordering controls, outboxes, dead-letter processes, correction propagation, replay runbooks, metrics, migration, and retirement evidence. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from occurrence semantics through identity, time, payload, schema, delivery, correction, protection, and replay. Ten examples, executable evidence, fifteen misconceptions, five exercises, and complete answers cover mechanics and assurance limitations.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, event-driven-architecture, distributed-systems, schema-language, broker, observability, security, privacy, legal, records-management, resilience, domain, or practitioner review is claimed.
